text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- All the basic issues which comprise the Cyprus problem will be put on the table during the first scheduled meeting between President Glafcos Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash.
- Criminals were trying to get involved in the creation of private security firms, taking advantage of loopholes in the law.
- Royal Marines have been banned from Cyprus after a naked pub frolic in Ayia Napa.
- Airport taxi drivers go on strike to protest against a government decision to issue new licences for town taxis.
- Leaders of communist Akel, socialist Edek and centre-left United Democrats appear confident of victory in next year's presidential election with Marios Eliades as their candidate.
- A team of experts will prepare documentation for the meeting between Clerides and Denktash in New York on July 9.
- Larnaca is split over the suggestion of the Cyprus Development Bank to create a company to administer the port in the town.
- Opposition parties make last-ditch attempts to find an opponent to Clerides in February's elections.
- Industrial peace hangs in the balance in commercial banks as talks between the bankers and their employees on the renewal of a collective agreement appear to be reaching a deadlock.
